about: Hand-written curation of the vendored Opengrep rule packs (ADR-0005 K.8, docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md section 13). scripts/build_opengrep_packs.py reads it with third_party/ and writes index.json and the pack folders. A drop group names rules by full rule ID (rules) or by path glob below this folder (paths); its kind and reason go into index.json.

packs.name: gitlab
packs.license: MIT and LGPL-3.0-only (the license header of each source file)

keep_only.reason: an LLM conversion of CodeQL queries without upstream tests: kalkan keeps only the rules that found a planted item of tests/fixtures/vulnapp without touching a secure twin or other code (Opengrep 1.30.1, 2026-11-07), and leaves out the GitHub Actions, secret and C rules that zizmor, Gitleaks, Kingfisher, flawfinder and the 0xdea pack already cover; the Rails mass assignment rule is left out too: it reports every X.new(params[...]), also ERB.new

cwe_classes.reason: configuration and debug settings, open listeners, permissions
SameSite cookies and HTTP verb confusion
Electron, WebView and app sandbox settings
authentication bypass and weak authentication mechanisms
sensitive data in cookies and headers
credentials and keys in source code
XSLT and XML injection, spreadsheet formulas, library search paths, environment from requests
Go struct tags that let a client set a field
container and cloud privileges, logging and key rotation
reverse tabnabbing navigates the opener page

language_classes.reason: every Solidity rule is a smart contract finding; the CWE (access control, input validation) would give a web class

drop.name: twin-false-positive
drop.reason: reports the secure twin of a planted item in tests/fixtures/vulnapp (Opengrep 1.30.1, 2026-10-25): the rule does not see the mitigation, and a verbatim pack cannot tune the rule text

drop.name: twin-false-positive-replacement-packs
drop.reason: reports the secure twin of a planted item in tests/fixtures/vulnapp (Opengrep 1.30.1, 2026-11-07): the rule does not see the mitigation (the njsscan originals of four GitLab ports that are dropped for the same reason, and two Java deserialization rules that also flag the look-ahead ObjectInputStream)

drop.name: noisy-comparisons-and-arguments
drop.reason: reports every comparison with a token-like name, or every fs call and RegExp with a non-literal argument, without data flow (eslint-plugin-security ports); on vulnapp the token comparisons of an arithmetic parser (node/lib/arith.js lines 24 and 31)

drop.name: noisy-every-use
drop.reason: reports every assert statement (Bandit B101), every use of the random module (Bandit B311) or every http:// link in HTML

drop.name: audit-markers
drop.reason: marks an endpoint, an import or a process start for manual review, without a dangerous argument or data flow (Bandit B4xx, B603, B605; find-sec-bugs JAXRS_ENDPOINT, JAXWS_ENDPOINT, COOKIE_USAGE, FORM_VALIDATE; any use of std::env::args, current_exe, temp_dir, argv or envp)

drop.name: not-security
drop.reason: performance, training correctness or code correctness without a security impact (PyTorch memory pinning and distributed waits, numpy distutils, data loader seeds, Go nil checks and map iteration, Rust panics, Ruby division by zero)

drop.name: hardening-advice
drop.reason: hardening advice or a reminder of a missing control (root, jailbreak and reverse-engineering detection, SafetyNet, screenshot and tapjacking protection, certificate pinning and transparency, keyboard cache, overlay protection, TLS 1.3, a minimum SDK level), not a vulnerability; njsscan good/* reports a present good control (helmet headers, CSRF and rate-limit middleware)

drop.name: not-security-android
drop.reason: Android code quality without a security impact: StrictMode in a release build, broadcast receivers that stay registered, static fields that keep an activity in memory

drop.name: covered-by-iac-and-cicd-tools
drop.reason: Kubernetes security contexts and network policies, and deprecated GitHub Actions workflow commands: Trivy, Checkov, zizmor and actionlint (which kalkan runs) already check them

drop.name: review-markers
drop.reason: marks an entry point, a framework class, a dependency or a code shape for manual review (INFO, mostly LOW confidence), without a dangerous argument or data flow: JAX-RS, Spring, Struts, ASP.NET, Express, Flask and Spark entry points, every exec or ProcessBuilder call, Velocity engines, and the review variants of the ORM leak rules

drop.name: join-mode
drop.reason: a join-mode rule: Opengrep 1.30.1 rejects it (opengrep validate: missing languages, mode join)

drop.name: noisy-logs-and-names
drop.reason: reports every log call, or every variable with a user-name or token-like name, without data flow (the GitLab port of the timing rule is dropped for the same reason)

drop.name: repeats-a-gitlab-port
drop.reason: the gitlab pack keeps its port (rules_lgpl_swift_other_rule-* and rules_lgpl_kotlin_other_rule-android-kotlin-webview-debug); the upstream pattern changed after the port, so the automatic duplicate check does not see the repeat

scope.reason: An Express request-handler rule (njsscan origin): in minified bundles almost every function of two or more parameters matches function($REQ, $RES, ...), and the match explodes. Measured 2026-10-27 on a large code base with Opengrep 1.30.1: this one rule took most of the pack matching time, and its only results in *.min.js were false positives inside vendored katex and bootstrap code (library-internal RegExp.test calls, no request input). The exclusion kept every other result and removed many timeouts. Vendored libraries stay covered by the vendored JavaScript check of sca match.
